To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose an unsupervized approach utilizing both text and student activity data to create Prerequisite Structure Graph for a given educational material, which outperformed the state-of-the-art supervised methods (which utilize only text content) and the human expert on the task of creating Prerequisite Structure Graph.

(1) we present an unsupervised algorithm that uses both text content and user data to create a Prerequisites Structure Graph (PSGs); (2) we propose an evaluation framework that uses a combination of human judgment and machine learning to evaluate the quality of PSGs; (3) we show that our algorithm performs significantly better compared to the supervised methods that use only text content.

(i) we can automatically generate PSGs from unstructured material and activity logs, (ii) we can use the PSGs for a variety of tasks, including finding the most effective path through the material for students to take and for instructors to teach, and (iii) our unsupervised approach to generate PSGs outperforms the supervised approach on the task of generating PSGs.
